panels.title: Market breadth today
panels.description:
Share of the tracked universe that closed up. Context for everything below, since a strong name in a weak market is a different proposition.

- **Breadth** — how widely a move is shared. Above 55% is broad strength, below 40% broad weakness.

targets.rawQueryText: SELECT ROUND(advancing_pct,1) AS "Advancing" FROM v_market_breadth ORDER BY session_date DESC LIMIT 1

panels.title: The 5 highest trend scores: a shortlist, not a forecast
panels.description:
The five highest scores among complete sessions, as of the last full session. A list to look at, not a prediction: nothing here knows how the market will open. Measured over a year of the whole liquid market, this score did not separate the next day's winners from its losers (see grafana/README.md), so read the scorecard underneath before leaning on the order.

- **Score** — distance above the 20-day average (%) + the 5-day return (%) + (RSI − 50) / 10, less a penalty above RSI 75.
- **RSI** — 0–100 momentum meter. Above 70 is conventionally overbought, which is why the score penalises it.
- **High / Low vs open** — averaged over this stock's last 20 complete sessions: how far above and below its own open it typically went.
- **Up / Down 1%+ days** — the share of those sessions in which it got 1% above, or 1% below, its open. A 0.6% or 1% sell target, and a stop, belong against these numbers.

Click a symbol to open its minute candles for today, from 9:15 to now.

targets.rawQueryText:
SELECT b.symbol                       AS "Symbol",
       ROUND(b.bullish_score, 2)            AS "Score",
       b.session_date                       AS "As of",
       b.open                               AS "Open",
       b.high                               AS "High",
       b.low                                AS "Low",
       b.close                              AS "Close",
       ROUND(b.pct_above_sma20, 2)          AS "vs SMA20 %",
       ROUND(b.ret5, 2)                     AS "5-day %",
       ROUND(b.rsi14, 1)                    AS "RSI(14)",
       ROUND(e.avg_high_vs_open_pct, 2)     AS "High vs open %",
       ROUND(e.avg_low_vs_open_pct, 2)      AS "Low vs open %",
       ROUND(e.pct_sessions_up_1, 0)        AS "Up 1%+ days %",
       ROUND(e.pct_sessions_down_1, 0)      AS "Down 1%+ days %",
       w.week52_high                        AS "52w high",
       w.week52_low                         AS "52w low",
       r.high_10                            AS "10d high",
       r.low_10                             AS "10d low",
       ROUND(r.pct_of_10d_range, 1)         AS "% of 10d range"
FROM v_bullish_ranking b
JOIN instrument i ON i.symbol = b.symbol
LEFT JOIN symbol_week52 w ON w.instrument_id = i.id
LEFT JOIN v_open_excursion e ON e.symbol = b.symbol
LEFT JOIN (SELECT symbol, high_10, low_10, pct_of_10d_range,
                  ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY symbol ORDER BY session_date DESC) AS rn
           FROM v_range_position) r ON r.symbol = b.symbol AND r.rn = 1
ORDER BY b.bullish_score DESC
LIMIT 5

panels.title: How the shortlist has done, scored on the session after each pick
panels.description:
Every evening's shortlist, scored on the next complete session of each pick. **Logged each evening** rows are the shortlists the nightly run wrote down; **Rebuilt from history** rows are the same ranking replayed over past sessions, so this page has a record from its first day.

- **Open→close** — what a buyer at the open would have made by the close, averaged over the picks. **vs avg** subtracts the same day's average over every symbol tracked here, so a rising market is not credited to the ranking.
- **Close→close** — the same from the previous close, so it includes the overnight gap.
- **Fell 1%+ below open** — the share of picks that dipped 1% under their open at some point in the session.

Averages that differ from zero by less than about 0.2 points are within the noise at this sample size. Empty until twenty sessions are stored and the first shortlist has a following session.

targets.rawQueryText:
SELECT CASE source WHEN 'live' THEN 'Logged each evening' ELSE 'Rebuilt from history' END AS "Shortlists",
       COUNT(DISTINCT as_of_date)                                      AS "Evenings",
       COUNT(*)                                                        AS "Picks scored",
       ROUND(AVG(gap_pct), 2)                                          AS "Avg gap %",
       ROUND(AVG(open_to_close_pct), 2)                                AS "Avg open→close %",
       ROUND(AVG(open_to_close_pct - market_open_to_close_pct), 2)     AS "Open→close vs avg (pts)",
       ROUND(AVG(close_to_close_pct - market_close_to_close_pct), 2)   AS "Close→close vs avg (pts)",
       ROUND(100.0 * AVG(open_to_close_pct > 0), 1)                    AS "Ended above open %",
       ROUND(100.0 * AVG(low_vs_open_pct <= -1), 1)                    AS "Fell 1%+ below open %"
FROM v_watchlist_outcome
GROUP BY source
ORDER BY source

panels.title: Bottom 10% of the 52-week range (or as far back as data goes)
panels.description:
Where price sits between its 52-week low and high, lowest first.

- **% of 52-week range** — 0 is at the year's low, 100 at its high.
- **% of 10-day range** — the same reading over ten sessions. Kept alongside because they answer different questions: ten sessions says where a stock sits this fortnight, a year says whether it is genuinely near a low.
- **Sessions behind it** — how many daily candles back the range. Well short of ~248 is not really a year.

Near a low is not the same as cheap: a name can sit there while it keeps falling.

Click a symbol to open its minute candles for today, from 9:15 to now.

targets.rawQueryText:
SELECT symbol                        AS "Symbol",
       close                              AS "Close",
       week52_low                         AS "52w low",
       week52_high                        AS "52w high",
       ROUND(pct_of_52w_range, 1)         AS "% of 52w range",
       ROUND(pct_of_10d_range, 1)         AS "% of 10d range",
       low_10                             AS "10d low",
       high_10                            AS "10d high",
       week52_sessions                    AS "Sessions behind it"
FROM v_range_context
WHERE pct_of_52w_range <= 10
ORDER BY pct_of_52w_range

panels.title: Bottom decile by value actually traded (10-day average)
panels.description:
The least liquid names, by rupees changing hands per day rather than by where price sits. Worth knowing before sizing a position in one of them.

- **Average daily turnover** — close × volume, averaged over the last 10 sessions.

Deliberately a 10-day window: liquidity is about what is trading now, not what traded last winter.

Click a symbol to open its minute candles for today, from 9:15 to now.

targets.rawQueryText:
WITH latest AS (
  SELECT symbol, close, avg_daily_turnover_10,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY symbol ORDER BY session_date DESC) AS rn
  FROM v_range_position),
current AS (SELECT * FROM latest WHERE rn = 1),
cutoff AS (SELECT avg_daily_turnover_10 AS threshold FROM current
           ORDER BY avg_daily_turnover_10
           LIMIT 1 OFFSET (SELECT CAST(COUNT(*) * 0.1 AS INTEGER) FROM current))
SELECT c.symbol                        AS "Symbol",
       c.close                         AS "Close",
       ROUND(c.avg_daily_turnover_10)  AS "Avg daily value traded (10d)"
FROM current c, cutoff
WHERE c.avg_daily_turnover_10 <= cutoff.threshold
ORDER BY c.avg_daily_turnover_10

panels.description: When a session's data was last written to the history these rankings are read from. That happens after the close - the daemon reconciles the day and evening.sh ingests it - so during the market day this shows that earlier write, not the live session. The 52-week band is a separate snapshot refreshed by hand, with its own as-of date in the table.

targets.rawQueryText: SELECT MAX(ingested_at) * 1000 AS "Last data refresh" FROM trading_day
